places.title: Green Bay, Wisconsin
places.summary: Born October 4, 1931, to William and Marie Stegmeier. His colleague’s memorial preserves the birthplace and date.

photo.alt: Downtown Green Bay reflected in the Fox River at dusk.
photo.title: Downtown Green Bay across the Fox River
photo.caption: A modern view across the Fox River toward downtown Green Bay.

places.title: Elgin, North Dakota
places.summary: The census finds eight-year-old Bill living with his parents and two younger sisters in Elgin. It also reports rural Grant County residence in 1935.

photo.alt: A black-and-white street photograph of the Elgin Hotel, a nearby automobile shop and parked vehicles in Elgin, North Dakota.
photo.title: The Elgin Hotel and neighboring storefronts
photo.caption: Elgin’s street scene in 1952, twelve years after the census found Bill’s family there.
photo.credit: Frank Agar Jr. · Noncommercial educational use. Image courtesy of the University of North Dakota.

places.title: Minneapolis, Minnesota
places.summary: The veterans register records his entry into the United States Marine Corps here on December 18, 1951.

photo.alt: The Stone Arch Bridge walkway leading toward the Minneapolis skyline.
photo.title: Minneapolis from the Stone Arch Bridge
photo.caption: The Mill District and downtown skyline, seen from the Stone Arch Bridge.

places.title: Yuma, Arizona
places.summary: Bill and Jean Cromer married in Yuma on January 2, 1953, during his Marine Corps years.

photo.alt: Historic storefronts, palm trees and a fountain in downtown Yuma.
photo.title: Downtown Yuma
photo.caption: Historic downtown Yuma, photographed decades after Bill and Jean’s wedding.

places.title: Camp Pendleton, California
places.summary: Records place him in a signal company at Camp Pendleton and later in a training regiment. He separated here as a corporal on December 3, 1953. A posting in Korea remains unestablished.

photo.alt: Camp Pendleton’s entrance road, gate sign and American flag.
photo.title: Camp Pendleton’s main entrance
photo.caption: The main entrance to Camp Pendleton, photographed in 1997.
photo.credit: SSGT RICHARD P. TUDOR, USMC · Public domain

places.title: Fort Collins, Colorado
places.summary: Bill earned bachelor’s and master’s degrees at Colorado State University. Their dates have not yet been established.

photo.alt: A walkway beneath mature trees beside the Oval lawn at Colorado State University.
photo.title: The Oval at Colorado State University
photo.caption: A tree-lined walk through the Oval on Colorado State’s Fort Collins campus.

places.title: Brookings, South Dakota
places.summary: A USDA report issued in February 1969 records that he had resumed graduate study at South Dakota State. It gives no exact enrollment or completion date.

photo.alt: The Administration Building and grounds at South Dakota State University.
photo.title: South Dakota State University campus
photo.caption: The Administration Building on South Dakota State’s Brookings campus.

places.title: Garden City, Kansas
places.summary: His Kansas State career began at Garden City in 1958. He studied familiar grains and possible alternative crops before moving to Hays.

photo.alt: The brick Southwest Research-Extension Center building and entrance sign in Garden City, Kansas.
photo.title: Southwest Research-Extension Center, Garden City
photo.caption: The research center at Garden City in a photograph published by K-State in 2025.
photo.credit: K-State Research and Extension · © Kansas State University

places.title: Hays, Kansas
places.summary: At Hays, Bill bred pearl millet and sunflower and explored other crops. He worked at the station from 1971 until his retirement in May 1998.

photo.alt: An aerial photograph of the Hays agricultural research station, with brick buildings, research plots, barns and shelterbelts.
photo.title: Agricultural Research Center–Hays from the air
photo.caption: An aerial view of the Hays research station in 2000, two years after Bill retired.
photo.credit: Kansas State University · © Kansas State University

crops.name: Pearl millet
crops.work: Bill selected for earlier flowering, shorter plants and larger seed. His breeding stocks became parents of hybrids grown in India.

parts.name: Grain head
parts.text: A dense, elongated head holds many small grains. Fine bristles give the head its bottle-brush outline.

parts.name: Leaf blades
parts.text: Long, narrow grass blades arch from the stem. The illustrations show each crop at its own scale.

parts.name: Jointed stem
parts.text: Leaves attach around the stem at sheathing bases. The joints are called nodes.

crops.name: Sunflower
crops.work: At Hays, Bill bred sunflower for better yields and resistance to insects and disease, helping develop it as a Kansas crop.

parts.name: Flower head
parts.text: What looks like one large flower is a head of many small flowers: yellow ray florets around a central disk of florets.

parts.name: Toothed leaves
parts.text: The broad leaves have toothed edges and distinct leaf stalks. Leaf shape changes with position on the plant.

parts.name: Stem
parts.text: The upright stem supports the leaves and heavy head. Cultivated sunflower forms vary in branching and head size.

crops.name: Canola
crops.work: Bill contributed to cooperative canola trials across the Great Plains, helping assess varieties under regional growing conditions.

parts.name: Four-petaled flowers
parts.text: Each flower has four yellow petals in a cross. Buds occur above open flowers as the flowering shoot grows.

parts.name: Slender seed pods
parts.text: Long, narrow pods develop below the flowers. Botanists call these pods siliques.

parts.name: Lower leaves
parts.text: Lower leaves are lobed and blue-green. Upper leaves are smaller and clasp the stem.

crops.name: Sorghum
crops.work: Sorghum was a familiar dryland comparison in millet trials. Bill also coauthored research on wheat streak mosaic virus in both crops.

parts.name: Branched grain head
parts.text: The grains sit on branches of a panicle. This drawing shows a compact grain type; panicle shape varies among sorghums.

parts.name: Grass blades
parts.text: Long grass blades spread from the upright stem. The leaf bases sheath the stem.

parts.name: Stem and nodes
parts.text: A sturdy jointed stem supports the grain head. Its nodes mark the points where leaves attach.
